input.summary: Ported reduction.cu/kernels.h to SYCL 2020 with no dpct helpers. Rewrote migrated/kernels.h as a single templated grid-stride kernel grid_stride_reduce<V> (V = 1,2,4,8,16) that ends in sycl::atomic_ref<int> fetch_add (relaxed, device scope, global space). Rewrote migrated/reduction.dp.cpp to use sycl::queue (in-order), sycl::malloc_device/sycl::free, a 1-D sycl::nd_range<1> per launch, and a run_benchmark<V> helper in place of the CUDA-style macro, with the same block sizes {128,256,512,1024}, the same blocks = min(ceil(n/bs), 2048) and blocks/V grid rule, and the same float64 output file. Compiled with icpx -fsycl and add_dpct_include=false: 0 errors, 0 warnings, so no dpct header is needed. Correctness: integer sums of 0/1 inputs with int atomics are order-independent and exact, so output should match the reference bit-for-bit; I did not execute the binary in this session (no run tool), so this is by construction, not measured.
